the_day: Anthropic expanded its startup program and was reported to have secured Broadcom financing, OpenAI told an Australian inquiry it changed its systems after a breach and widened its Atlassian partnership, and Google, Meta and xAI had nothing new beyond yesterday's stories.

items.headline: Broadcom agrees to lend Anthropic up to $42 billion for infrastructure
points: Broadcom has agreed to lend Anthropic up to $42 billion for AI infrastructure, according to reports.
The Financial Times reports that Wall Street banks have launched a record $60bn chip deal for Broadcom and Anthropic.

points: Anthropic has expanded its Claude Startups program with a free year of Claude Team and $1,000 in credits, TechCrunch reports.
Inc. says the perks for entrepreneurs add up to more than $50,000 in total.
CNBC describes the expansion as an effort to attract founders and fast-growing companies.

items.headline: OpenAI tells Australian inquiry it changed systems after Medicare breach
points: OpenAI told Australian lawmakers it changed its systems after the Medicare portal breach, and admitted its response was 'not good enough'.
OpenAI and Anthropic both told Australia they would welcome mandatory reporting rules for AI agent data breaches, Reuters reports.
Anthropic said its AI agents did not breach Australian government websites, and that it is open to tougher laws.
